# Overlays

From [the component index](../components.md). A prop with `?` is optional, and `= x` is its default. An indented line is the shape of a value the prop takes. In the examples, `children`, `transactions`, the icons and the handlers stand for the screen's own content, data and state.

## Sheet

```tsx
import { Sheet } from "@tuja/ui/components/sheet";
```

A modal for a short task, such as a form to add or edit one thing; a bottom sheet on a phone.

Props (also `css`):

- `children?: ReactNode` — The sheet's content. The card pads it, fits its height up to the viewport and scrolls it beyond that.
- `isOpen: boolean` — Whether the sheet is shown; the consumer owns this state.
- `onClose: () => void` — Called when the user asks to close the sheet: Escape, a click on the dimmed page, the close button, or a drag down.
- `closeLabel: string` — Accessible label for the close button.
- `closeIcon?: ReactNode` — Icon rendered inside the close button.
- `initialFocusRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>` — Element to focus when the sheet opens.
- `liftFrom?: () => HTMLElement | null` — Below `md`, the element the card lifts out of, such as the row that opened it.
- `onProgress?: (progress: number) => void` — Called on each frame that the card or the dimmed page moves, with how far the card is in: 0 away and 1 at rest.
- `title?: ReactNode` — The sheet's title. It shares the top row with the close button, which it never runs under, and it names the dialog.
- `aria-label?: string` — Accessible name for the dialog.
- `aria-labelledby?: string` — Id of a visible element that names the dialog.

Example:

```tsx
function SheetExample() {
  return (
    <Sheet
      isOpen={isOpen}
      onClose={close}
      closeLabel="Close"
      title="Add to calendar"
    >
      <div css={stack.item}>{children}</div>
    </Sheet>
  );
}
```

## Popover

```tsx
import { Popover } from "@tuja/ui/components/popover";
```

Non-modal content hung off a trigger, such as details or a small form; for commands use `MenuButton`.

Props (also `css`):

- `children: ReactNode` — Popover content. Anything — this is not a menu.
- `trigger: (props: PopoverTriggerProps) => ReactNode` — Renders the trigger: spread the supplied props onto whatever element opens the popover (a `Button`, a bare `<button>`) to wire up the anchor ref, open state, and ARIA.
- `placement?: "top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left" | "top-start" | "top-end" | "right-start" | "right-end" | "bottom-start" | "bottom-end" | "left-start" | "left-end" = "bottom-start"` — Preferred side and alignment: `"top"`, `"right"`, `"bottom"` or `"left"`, each also available as `-start` and `-end`.
- `offset?: number = 8` — Gap between trigger and popover, in pixels.
- `portalTarget?: Element | DocumentFragment | null` — Where to render the portal, which is what keeps the popover out of a clipping or transformed ancestor.
- `aria-label?: string` — Accessible name for the popover.
- `aria-labelledby?: string` — Id of a visible element that names the popover, instead of the trigger.
- `ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>` — Ref to the popover element, merged with the one placement needs.
- `open?: boolean` — Controlled open state. Requires `onOpenChange`.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void` — Called with the next state on every open or close.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean` — Initial open state when uncontrolled; ignored once `open` is supplied.

Example:

```tsx
function PopoverExample() {
  return (
    <Popover
      trigger={(triggerProps) => (
        <Button {...triggerProps} look="outline" size="sm">
          Details
        </Button>
      )}
    >
      <Text look="bodySmall">{children}</Text>
    </Popover>
  );
}
```
